column1: # Ruling R261 (14 Nov 2026, the second trust audit's finding G6, BUILD-LOG's Morocco owner question 5): the Ministry of
# Habous's own month tables for Sebta (ville 24) and Melilla (ville 40), held to the promise alone at the app's Ceuta
# and Melilla and at Habous's own points for them (a `-promise.tsv` file, GateRow.promiseOnly: an early start or a late
# end breaks the gate; no late limit applies, the days are in no stamp). Kept by hand: `generateEnvelopeRows` neither
# writes nor removes this file.
# Why: the app places Ceuta and Melilla in Spain, whose safe default (default.safe.europe, its 18° dawn less 2 min)
# ended the fast 2 to 3 min after the Fajr Habous prints for the two cities on every held day. Habous prints a table
# for each, and the cities' Muslims may well pray by it, so within 10 km of either table's point its own day rides
# beside Spain's (Maghreb.spainAt): never a start before it, nor sunrise or the end of eating after it. The lateness
# against it (Spain's Fajr is the 12° family's, its Isha the 18° one) is the region's design and no figure here.
# Splits. November 2026 is the month the tables' points, horizons and sunrise and Maghrib seconds were read on
# (HabousCities.spain, habous_units.py spain-rows and spain-build): fit. October 2026 was held out: test. The tables
# are printed in UTC (the clock column). Coordinates and the tables' own paths only, never a time.
# What these rows hold: October and November 2026, no more. The monitor does not read villes 24 and 40, so December
# onward (Ramadan 1448 included) rests on November's fit and no row checks it against Habous's print until a later
# month is held and added here.
